desk.headline: Adjusted EPS nearly doubles to C$1.65, beat; net debt target hit, all free cash flow now to go to buybacks
results: Adjusted earnings rose to C$3.4bn (C$1.65 a share) from C$1.8bn as WTI averaged US$85.68 against US$64.95 a year ago; reported net earnings were C$3.0bn.
Adjusted funds flow climbed 41% to C$5.5bn and free cash flow was about C$2.1bn.
Output of 1.65m boe/d was up 2%, with record thermal in situ (about 300,000 bbl/d) and record conventional liquids; oil sands mining volumes dipped during the Horizon turnaround.
Net debt fell to C$12.1bn, below the C$13bn target; C$2.9bn went back to shareholders in the quarter (C$1.3bn dividends, C$1.6bn buybacks).
Quarterly dividend held at C$0.625, payable 5 Jan 2027.

guidance.summary: The results release gives no new production or spending ranges; it says the company is on track with its 2026 budget. With the debt target met, it now aims to put 100% of free cash flow into share buybacks, about C$800m a month in Nov–Dec.

watch: Whether buybacks run at the C$800m-a-month pace and the 100% free-cash-flow policy holds into 2027.
Horizon output after the turnaround finished early (about 640,000 bbl/d now) and the move to a three-year turnaround cycle.
Oil prices: WTI was down from US$92.85 in Q2 to US$85.68 in Q3.
